# Partner Compensation Reconciliation — Usage Guide

*Mode: direct · 🔌 offline (no LLM)*

Takes one financial year's partner-compensation documents -- the monthly payout advices, the Compensation Advisory letter, and optionally the LLP's own capital-account statement, a GnuCash book (read only), and a 26AS workbook -- and cross-checks the figures they carry against each other. Every rate, percentage and period this skill uses (the firm's-tax rate, the capital-contribution rate, the capital accretion period, the remuneration-TDS section/rate/start-date) comes from that year's own entity/tax-rules config, never hardcoded, since all of them change by year and the capital rate has been known to change mid-year. A missing rate or a missing source figure produces an explicit "cannot reconcile" row naming what is missing, never a default or a silently-assumed match. The two required documents (the monthly advices and the Advisory) and the optional LLP statement of account now parse for real; a document that fails to open/parse (unreadable/malformed PDF, wrong password, or content that doesn't match the expected layout) still fails the whole run loud, naming the document and the reason (the LLP statement is the exception, since it is optional -- see its own gotcha below). Every optional document's leg (the LLP statement, the incentive payment schedule, the GnuCash books tie-out, the 26AS TDS-credit tie-out) degrades to an explicit "not available" note when its input is absent, or when its document fails to parse -- every one of these readers is real and implemented (see AGENT.md), not a placeholder.

## When to use it

Use this once a financial year's partner-compensation documents are in hand and you want a single reconciliation across remuneration, share of profit, the incentive cohort ledger, capital contribution, one-offs, and (if relevant) a payroll stint -- particularly useful for catching a mid-year capital-rate change (which shows up as unequal capital-deducted amounts within one incentive cohort) or a one-off incentive that was grossed up at the wrong year's tax rate. Not a substitute for tax computation or return preparation -- it only reconciles the streams against each other and the return's own figures; it does not compute tax due.

## Inputs

- **Monthly partner payout certificates / payslips** (required) — accepts: One or more PDF files.
  - All of this financial year's monthly payout certificates / payslips, as PDFs.
  - ⚠️ Required. Each PDF is dispatched on its CONTENT, never its filename, to the monthly payout-advice parser -- a PDF that fails to open/parse, or whose content doesn't match that layout, fails the whole run loud, naming the file and the reason.
- **Entity** (required) — accepts: One of the entities defined in entities.yaml, via dropdown.
  - The partner/entity this reconciliation is for.
  - ⚠️ Required -- also selects the GnuCash book below when one is registered for this entity.
- **Document password (optional -- if the advices/advisory PDFs are protected)** (optional) — accepts: The PDFs' own open password, if any.
  - Password for the payout advices / advisory PDFs, if they are protected.
  - ⚠️ Optional -- leave blank if the PDFs are not password-protected. Never logged, never included in any output file.
- **Compensation advisory / target compensation advice** (required) — accepts: A single PDF file.
  - The firm's Compensation Advisory / target compensation advice letter for this financial year.
  - ⚠️ Required. Shares a directory with the monthly payout advices at some firms -- this skill dispatches on document CONTENT, never filename, since filenames are not a reliable way to tell the two document families apart. A PDF that fails to open/parse, or whose content doesn't match the Advisory's expected layout, fails the whole run loud, naming the file and the reason.
- **LLP statement of account (enables leg 1, the capital sign-off)** (optional) — accepts: A single PDF file.
  - The LLP's own statement of account for this partner, this financial year.
  - ⚠️ Optional -- enables the capital sign-off leg (leg 1). Absent, or supplied but unreadable/malformed/not actually an LLP statement of account (wrong document filed here), this leg degrades to an explicit "not available" note naming the reason; it never fails the whole run and never falls back to a zero or a default. The statement is often issued months after the financial year ends, so it is common for it to be genuinely unavailable at filing time.
- **Incentive payment schedule (enables the schedule leg -- takes precedence over the payout advices when both agree, and reports any disagreement)** (optional) — accepts: A single PDF file.
  - The firm's own incentive payment schedule for this financial year (the L4 document).
  - ⚠️ Optional -- enables the schedule leg, and takes PRECEDENCE over the payout advices for gross share of profit and both firm's-tax figures (firm_tax_on_sop, firm_tax_others) when supplied. Absent, or supplied but unreadable/malformed/not actually a payment schedule, this leg degrades to an explicit "not available" note naming the reason; it never fails the whole run. A disagreement between the schedule and a payout advice is reported as a diagnostic note, not a run failure.
- **GnuCash book (READ ONLY -- enables the books tie-out)** (optional) — accepts: GnuCash XML book (.gnucash), optionally gzip-compressed.
  - This entity's GnuCash book, opened READ ONLY for the books tie-out.
  - ⚠️ Optional. Never opened for writing by this skill. Absent (or unreadable/malformed), the books tie-out leg is reported 'not available', never defaulted.
- **26AS workbook (enables the TDS-credit tie-out)** (optional) — accepts: Excel (.xlsx) with a Part I (TDS) sheet.
  - 26AS workbook produced by this repo's '26AS' skill, for the same entity/year.
  - ⚠️ Optional. Absent (or unreadable/malformed), the TDS-credit tie-out leg is reported 'not available', never defaulted.
- **GnuCash journal CSV output path (optional -- Stage 1b)** (optional) — accepts: A full output file path ending in .csv.
  - Optional. When set, also writes a GnuCash multi-split journal CSV of the year's implied journal entries (Stage 1b) to this path -- one monthly-payout transaction per month, plus an opening reclassification entry if the input's opening_reclass: block is present. Leave blank to only produce the workbook.
  - ⚠️ Requires an accounts: block naming the GnuCash account for every non-zero split (bank, tds_expense, interest_on_capital, current_account, capital_contribution, medical_expense, remuneration_income, share_of_profit_income) -- a missing account needed by a non-zero month comes back as an "ERROR: ..." naming the key and the month, not a traceback. As of H35-05 round 2: the journal CSV is ONLY ever written when a GnuCash book (with accounts.bank present and resolvable in it) is also supplied, so this run's cash leg can be matched against what the bank import already posted rather than booking a second, unconditional bank leg. Whenever matching cannot run for any reason -- no gnucash_path, no accounts.bank configured, the book cannot be read, or accounts.bank's path is not found in the book -- the journal CSV is refused with an "ERROR: cannot write the journal CSV -- ..." message naming the reason, and NO file is written at all, even a partial one. The recon workbook (and the accrual journal from accrual_journal_path, below, which has no bank leg and is unaffected) are still written as normal in this case -- only the monthly journal CSV is refused.
- **Year-end share-of-profit accrual journal CSV output path (optional -- H35-02, requires journal_path and the LLP statement of account)** (optional) — accepts: A full output file path ending in .csv, different from journal_path.
  - Optional (H35-02). Requires journal_path to also be set. When set, and the LLP statement of account (llp_statement) parsed and its "Profit Share for the Year" figure is available, writes a SEPARATE one-transaction CSV -- never merged into journal_path's file -- dated 31 March of the financial year's END year (e.g. FY "2025-26" -> 2026-03-31, never the FY start year), accruing the difference between the L5 statement's own year-end profit-share figure and the total already booked by the monthly journal (Dr current_account / Cr share_of_profit_income). No file is written, and a note explains why, when: no LLP statement was supplied or it didn't parse; its profit-share figure is missing; the difference is within Rs 1.00 (already ties); or the difference is negative (the monthly total already booked exceeds the L5 figure -- FLAGGED for manual review, never reversed automatically).
  - ⚠️ Reuses the same accounts: block as journal_path -- specifically current_account and share_of_profit_income must both be supplied. A residual current-account comparison against the L5 statement is always performed after this accrual and reported in the run summary; it is never booked, even when it shows a variance.
- **Bank-match date window in days (optional -- H35-05, default 7)** (optional) — accepts: A whole number of days, e.g. 7 or 14.
  - Optional (H35-05). How many days either side of a monthly payout's month-end date to look for a matching bank credit already posted in the book. Defaults to 7 when left blank or unparsable.
  - ⚠️ Only used when both gnucash_path and accounts.bank are available and resolvable in the book. As of H35-05 round 2, that availability is no longer optional for journal_path: when a book cannot be used for matching (missing, unreadable, or accounts.bank absent/not found in it) AND journal_path was requested, the journal CSV is refused outright rather than falling back to the pre-H35-05 unconditional bank leg -- see journal_path's own gotchas above. The recon workbook alone (no journal_path) still runs and reports the bank-match leg as "not available" in that case, exactly as before. When a book IS available: each payout is matched to a bank credit within Re 1 and within this window, one-to-one, nearer date wins; two equally-close candidates are NEVER auto-picked -- that payout gets no journal and is flagged TIE (candidates listed) instead. A deposit split across two or more counter-accounts is also never auto-picked -- that payout gets no journal and is flagged SPLIT (naming every counter-account the bank import spread it across), distinct from a genuine NO_MATCH gap, since a matching credit WAS found, just not one this skill can route a single journal leg to. A matched payout's cash leg posts to the bank import's OWN counter-account for that credit, never a second leg on the bank account itself. See the workbook's "Bank match" sheet and the run summary's "BANK MATCH" block for full detail, per payout.

## How to run

1. Pick the entity.
2. Pick this financial year's monthly payout advices (one or more PDFs) and the Compensation Advisory letter.
3. Optionally supply the LLP statement, the incentive payment schedule, a GnuCash book, and/or a 26AS workbook to enable their tie-out legs.
4. Click Run.
5. Download the workbook and review the Reconciliation and Exceptions sheets first, then Capital for any mid-year rate-change warning.

## Output

Output is written to the **`Data/outputs/`** folder, named:

```
Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-partner-comp-recon.xlsx
```

Files produced:

- **`YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-partner-comp-recon.xlsx`** — Ten sheets: Logic (the seven reconciled legs and the governing identity, in prose), Drivers (every rate/period/date as a labelled input cell -- the only sheet where one appears as a literal), Monthly grid, Payroll stream (only present if the input supplied payroll months), One-offs (the gross-up and its roundness check), Cohorts (the incentive ledger with its reporting/prior/future FY-assignment column), Capital (the rule as a formula off Drivers, the Advisory cross-check, and the mid-year rate-change detector), Reconciliation (agree / variance / cannot-reconcile per category -- topped by a highlighted "STATEMENT DISAGREES" block when the LLP Statement of Account disagrees with another source or fails its own arithmetic; see the tip below), Exceptions (every non-agreeing or non-reconcilable row collected together), and Open items (anything left unresolved and what would close it). A "Bank match" sheet (H35-05) is also added whenever a GnuCash book and accounts.bank are both available: one row per monthly payout showing which bank credit already posted in the book it matched to (date/amount/account), or why it did not (no bank credit found, a TIE naming every equally-close candidate, or a SPLIT naming every counter-account a matching-but-unroutable deposit was spread across).
- **`<journal_path> (optional -- Stage 1b, only written if journal_path is set)`** — A GnuCash multi-split journal CSV: one balanced transaction per monthly payout (dated month-end), plus an opening reclassification entry if opening_reclass: was supplied. Import via File > Import > Import Transactions from CSV with Multi-split ticked, skipping the 1 header line, Date mapped as ISO, and the Amount column mapped to the importer's Amount column type.
- **`<accrual_journal_path> (optional -- H35-02, only written if accrual_journal_path is set AND an accrual was computed)`** — A SEPARATE one-transaction GnuCash multi-split journal CSV, dated 31 March of the financial year's END year (e.g. FY "2025-26" -> 2026-03-31): the year-end share-of-profit accrual per the LLP statement of account. Same import settings as journal_path's file, above. Never contains the monthly transactions -- import both files if both were produced.

## Tips

Start with the Reconciliation sheet, then Exceptions -- a "CANNOT RECONCILE" status names exactly which source figure for that category was not supplied, so a "cannot reconcile" row is something to fix in the input, not a defect in the workbook. On Capital, a "RATE CHANGE SUSPECTED" row means the incentive cohort's instalments show unequal capital-deducted amounts -- re-read that year's Compensation Advisory, since it will have been reissued at a new rate part-way through the cohort. The LLP Statement of Account (L5), when supplied, is the REFERENCE for every row it carries a figure for (closing capital, current-account closing, remuneration, interest on capital, profit share, drawings) -- every other source is measured against it, never averaged in as an equal peer. Any disagreement beyond the Re 1 tolerance, or a failure in the statement's own arithmetic, is flagged both at the top of the run summary text and in a highlighted "STATEMENT DISAGREES" block above the Reconciliation sheet's table -- check that block first, before the per-row statuses below it.

## Troubleshooting

| If… | Then… |
|------|-------|
| A category shows 'CANNOT RECONCILE' with a reason naming a driver or a figure. | That figure isn't available for this financial year -- this skill never guesses or falls back to a prior year's value. |
| A 'STATEMENT DISAGREES' block appears at the top of the run summary / Reconciliation sheet. | The LLP Statement of Account (L5) is the reference for that row, and another supplied source (or the statement's own printed arithmetic) disagrees with it beyond the Re 1 tolerance -- the note spells out 'Statement says X; <source> says Y; difference Z' or names the failed arithmetic check. Investigate the disagreement; this skill never picks a winner for you. |
| 'Total cash received (monthly payouts) vs Bank' still shows 'NOT CHECKED YET (bank credits are matched in H35-05)'. | As of H35-05, this row is only left as NOT CHECKED YET when there is nothing to check against -- no GnuCash book was supplied, or no accounts.bank is configured for this entity. Whenever both are available, this row is replaced with a real per-payout bank match result: AGREE when every monthly payout matched a bank credit already posted in the book (within Re 1 and the bank_match_window), or CANNOT RECONCILE naming how many payouts did not (see the 'BANK MATCH' block in the run summary and the workbook's 'Bank match' sheet for the per-payout detail, including any TIE candidates). |
| The run summary shows a 'BANK MATCH -- N payout(s) could not be matched...' block, or the 'Bank match' sheet shows NO_MATCH / TIE / SPLIT rows. | NO_MATCH means no bank credit within Re 1 and bank_match_window days of that payout's month-end date was found in the book at all -- a genuine gap, never silently booked; investigate the bank statement/book for that period. TIE means two or more equally-close bank credits qualified and none was auto-picked (the user's ruling: a tie is never auto-picked) -- the candidates are listed with date/amount/account; either narrow bank_match_window, or resolve the ambiguity in the book, then re-run. SPLIT (H35-05 round 2) means a matching credit WAS found, but the bank import posted it across two or more counter-accounts, so there is no single account to route this skill's journal leg to -- the counter-accounts are named; this is never reported as a genuine gap (a credit did match) and is never auto-routed to any one of them. None of NO_MATCH / TIE / SPLIT ever gets a journal line for that payout's cash leg -- see journal_path's output, which simply omits that month's transaction rather than guessing (the OTHER, matched payouts' journal lines are written normally). This is different from matching being UNAVAILABLE altogether (no book, no accounts.bank, an unreadable book, or accounts.bank not found in it) -- that case is a structural refusal, not a per-payout gap, and as of H35-05 round 2 it refuses the WHOLE journal CSV with an ERROR rather than falling back to the pre-H35-05 unconditional bank leg -- see journal_path's own gotchas. |
| The D1 drawings row ('Current-account drawings: statement vs (net monthly payouts + TDS + other payslip deductions - gross interest on capital)') shows a gap I can't explain. | The identity is: statement current drawings = net monthly payouts + s.194T TDS withheld + other payslip deductions paid on the partner's behalf (e.g. medical top-up) - interest on capital, GROSS. Interest on capital is credited to/drawn from the CAPITAL column of the LLP Statement, not the current account, so it is backed OUT of this current-account identity -- and it must be the GROSS figure, not the net-of-its-own-s.194T-TDS amount that lands in the payout (that TDS is already inside the TDS total above, so subtracting the net figure would double-count it). The row's note spells out the full build-up (each component and its value) so you can see exactly where a gap comes from. |
| A row's note starts with 'PENDING JOURNAL POSTING (provided by this skill)'. | This is not a disagreement. The Statement and the books gap by more than Re 1 today, but this skill's own not-yet-posted journal (its monthly lines or its year-end share-of-profit accrual) closes that gap to within Re 1 once posted -- the note names the journal id(s) and amount. Post the journal(s) named and the row is reconciled; nothing further to investigate. If posting the journal only closes PART of the gap, the row instead reports the genuine residual left over (as a normal disagreement) rather than the pre-journal gap or this pending-journal wording. |
| A GnuCash tie-out row (bank, TDS, interest on capital, current account, capital contribution, medical expense, remuneration income, or share of profit income) shows 'PENDING JOURNAL POSTING (provided by this skill)' instead of a plain AGREE/VARIANCE. | Same rule as the L5 rows above, extended to every GnuCash tie-out row: when this run's own posted-check finds that account's monthly journal not yet posted in the book, the row is compared against the book PLUS that journal rather than the book alone, and is reconciled once the named journal id(s) are posted. A row on 'current_account' or 'capital_contribution' may also name a separately posted prior-period reclassification journal (Num starting with this firm-FY's prefix, e.g. '<FIRM>-<FY>-RECT') -- that journal is a real posted movement from capital to the current account from an earlier run of this skill, folded into the computed side as its own named line, never counted toward a variance. |
| 'Exempt share of profit (s.10(2A)) vs the filed return' shows 'NOT CHECKED (return not supplied)' instead of AGREE. | This is expected, not a defect. The LLP Statement's Profit Share for the Year is present and correct -- only the comparison against the filed income tax return is skipped because the return wasn't supplied. It never counts as a failure and never appears in the 'STATEMENT DISAGREES' block; supply the filed return to get an actual comparison. |
| 'Incentive instalments: award-year Advisory vs payment schedule' note now starts with 'INFORMATIONAL (superseded by ...)'. | This category is no longer the primary drawings check -- see the new 'Current-account drawings: statement vs (net monthly payouts + s.194T TDS withheld)' row for that. This one still reports a genuine Advisory-vs-schedule disagreement when it fires; it is informational, not retired. |
| Reconciliation shows AGREE for two sources that are not byte-for-byte equal. | Every reconciliation in this skill (including the L5 tie-out rows) uses a Re 1 tolerance: two sources within Rs 1.00 of each other tie, anything more is reported as VARIANCE. This is a fixed, named constant (engine.RECONCILIATION_TOLERANCE), never a per-run setting -- it absorbs paisa-level rounding between sources, not a genuine discrepancy. |
| Reconciliation shows VARIANCE on the incentive schedule leg. | A VARIANCE means the supplied payment schedule and a payout advice genuinely disagree on gross share of profit or a firm's-tax figure for that month -- check the Note column for the exact numbers. The schedule's own figure is what is used; the disagreement is reported, not silently resolved. |
| 'ERROR: could not parse ...' naming the advisory letter or a payout advice. | The PDF is unreadable/malformed, password-protected without the right password, or its content doesn't match the expected layout (e.g. an L1 payout certificate misfiled as the Advisory) -- fix the underlying document/password, not the filename. |
| Incentive payment schedule leg shows 'not available' even though payment_schedule was supplied. | The document failed to open/parse, or its content didn't match the payment schedule's expected layout -- the reason is named in the note itself; this leg degrades rather than failing the run, so check the note text and re-supply the correct document. |
| LLP capital sign-off leg (leg 1) shows 'not available' even though llp_statement was supplied. | The document failed to open/parse, or its content didn't match the LLP Statement of Account layout (e.g. it doesn't carry a combined CAPITAL ACCOUNT / CURRENT ACCOUNT header and a 'STATEMENT OF ACCOUNT OF ... AS ON <date> MARCH, <year>' phrase) -- the reason is named in the note itself; this leg degrades rather than failing the run, so check the note text and re-supply the correct document. |
